images.prompt: A bell-shaped curve representing the sampling distribution of a test statistic (e.g., Z-score or T-score) under the null hypothesis. The center of the distribution is at the value predicted by H0. Label the x-axis as 'Test Statistic Value' and the y-axis as 'Probability Density'. An arrow points from the center to a hypothetical observed test statistic value, illustrating deviation from H0.

images.prompt: A bell-shaped curve showing the sampling distribution under the null hypothesis. Shade the two tails of the distribution, representing the critical regions for a two-tailed test. Label the area of each shaded tail as $\alpha/2$. Clearly mark the critical values on the x-axis that define the start of these shaded regions. An arrow points to the total shaded area, labeled as $\alpha$.

images.prompt: Two overlapping bell curves. The left curve represents the sampling distribution under the null hypothesis ($H_0$), centered at $\mu_0$. The right curve represents the sampling distribution under a specific alternative hypothesis ($H_1$), centered at $\mu_1$. Shade the rejection region (alpha) in the tail of the $H_0$ distribution. Then, shade the area under the $H_1$ distribution that falls within this rejection region, labeling it as 'Power (1-beta)'. The unshaded portion of the $H_1$ curve within the non-rejection region of $H_0$ should be labeled 'Beta (Type II Error)'.
